slots.sample: Since 1982, RES has welcomed Brooklyn to one of the neighborhood’s oldest buildings, at ((a href="https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=4+5th+Avenue%2C+Brooklyn%2C+NY+11217" target="_blank" rel="noopener" title="Open in Google Maps"))4 5th Avenue at St. Marks Place, Cathedral District((/a)). Our kitchen cooks seasonal market produce over a wood fire, the bar pours local beer and classic cocktails, and every table gets the same warm welcome, whether you drop in for a quick lunch or stay for a long dinner.
slots.label: Welcome to RES Bar & Restaurant / hero-intro
Welcome to RES Bar & Restaurant / hero-img

slots.sample: RES opened its doors on 5th Avenue in 1982 as a twelve-table neighborhood bar with a short menu and a long wine list. Four decades later the room is bigger and the kitchen busier, but the idea is the same: honest food cooked from scratch, drinks poured generously and a dining room where regulars and first-timers are greeted the same way. Many of our suppliers have been with us for more than twenty years, and our recipes still start with what the farmers bring in each morning.
slots.label: Features Intro / description

slots.sample: Our chefs build every plate around the season: spring peas and ramps, summer tomatoes, autumn squash and slow braises through the winter. Breads are baked in-house every morning, pasta is rolled by hand and fish arrives daily from the Fulton market. Pair it with a cocktail from the bar or a bottle from our cellar, and let our team take care of the rest.
slots.label: Features Intro / description

slots.sample: Great food brings guests in the first time; great service is what brings them back. After four decades on 5th Avenue, these are the four habits our floor team practises every single shift.
slots.label: 4 Habits That Can Improve Your Customer Service

slots.sample: Greet every table within a minute.
slots.label: 4 Habits That Can Improve Your Customer Service

slots.sample: Even on the busiest Friday night, a quick hello and a glass of water tells guests they have been seen. The order can wait a moment; the welcome cannot.
slots.label: 4 Habits That Can Improve Your Customer Service

slots.sample: Know the menu like a cook.
slots.label: 4 Habits That Can Improve Your Customer Service

slots.sample: Our servers taste every new dish before it goes on the menu, so they can explain what is in it, how it is cooked and what to drink with it, and answer allergy questions with confidence.
slots.label: 4 Habits That Can Improve Your Customer Service

slots.sample: Listen more than you talk, and close the loop.
slots.label: 4 Habits That Can Improve Your Customer Service

slots.sample: When something is not right we fix it at the table, then tell the kitchen so it does not happen again. A complaint handled well often turns a guest into a regular.
slots.label: 4 Habits That Can Improve Your Customer Service

slots.sample: 4 Habits That Can Improve Your Customer Service
slots.label: 4 Habits That Can Improve Your Customer Service

slots.sample: Fast-casual chains keep testing new concepts, and a burger spinoff from a burrito brand is the latest sign that the category is still hungry for growth.
slots.label: Chipotle to launch burger spinoff this fall

slots.sample: For neighborhood restaurants the lesson is not to chase the trend but to understand what guests are asking for: fresh ingredients, a short menu they can trust and food that arrives quickly without tasting rushed.
slots.label: Chipotle to launch burger spinoff this fall

slots.sample: Our own burger has been on the menu since 1982. We grind the beef in-house every morning, toast the buns to order and keep the toppings simple. Sometimes the best answer to a new trend is to keep doing one thing very well.
slots.label: Chipotle to launch burger spinoff this fall

slots.sample: Chipotle to launch burger spinoff this fall
slots.label: Chipotle to launch burger spinoff this fall

slots.sample: Kitchens are famous for long hours and little rest. Keeping a talented chef means taking their time off as seriously as their time on the line.
slots.label: How To Help Your Chef Achieve A Better Work-Life Balance

slots.sample: At RES we plan the rota four weeks ahead, give every cook two consecutive days off and close the kitchen for a full week each January. Prep lists are shared so no one person carries the whole service, and the sous chef runs the pass two nights a week so the head chef can go home to their family.
slots.label: How To Help Your Chef Achieve A Better Work-Life Balance

slots.sample: The result is a calmer kitchen, fewer mistakes and a team that has stayed with us for years. Guests may never see it, but they taste it in every plate.
slots.label: How To Help Your Chef Achieve A Better Work-Life Balance

slots.sample: How To Help Your Chef Achieve A Better Work-Life Balance
slots.label: How To Help Your Chef Achieve A Better Work-Life Balance

slots.sample: Independent restaurants are being offered more apps, tablets and dashboards than ever, yet many owners remain unconvinced that every new screen makes the dining room better.
slots.label: Indies aren't sold on tech

slots.sample: Technology earns its place when it saves time for the team or makes life easier for the guest: online reservations, a reliable card terminal at the table, a kitchen display that keeps tickets in order. It loses its place when it gets between the server and the guest.
slots.label: Indies aren't sold on tech

slots.sample: We use a simple booking system and a kitchen printer that has not missed a ticket in years. Everything else we judge by one question: does it help us look after the people in front of us?
slots.label: Indies aren't sold on tech

slots.sample: When a coffee giant hires an executive from a sportswear brand, it is a reminder that restaurant brands are as much about experience and loyalty as they are about the product in the cup.
slots.label: Starbucks brings Under Armour exec on board

slots.sample: Big chains borrow ideas from retail: loyalty programmes, mobile ordering and carefully designed stores. Small restaurants can borrow too, at a human scale. Remembering a regular’s usual order is still the best loyalty programme there is.
slots.label: Starbucks brings Under Armour exec on board

slots.sample: At RES our bartenders know hundreds of guests by name and by drink. No app can replace that, but it is worth watching how the big players think about the whole journey from the front door to the last sip.
slots.label: Starbucks brings Under Armour exec on board

slots.sample: Starbucks brings Under Armour exec on board
slots.label: Starbucks brings Under Armour exec on board

slots.sample: Ideas that start in fine-dining kitchens tend to reach everyday menus a few years later. Here are eight we are seeing on menus across the country, and in our own kitchen.
slots.label: 8 trends trickling down to mainstream menus

slots.sample: 1. Vegetables as the main course, not the side. 2. Fermentation: house pickles, kimchi and hot sauces. 3. Wood-fired cooking for smoke and char. 4. Smaller plates made for sharing.
slots.label: 8 trends trickling down to mainstream menus

slots.sample: 5. Global breakfast dishes served all day. 6. Low- and no-alcohol cocktails with as much care as the classics. 7. Heritage grains in breads and salads. 8. Menus that name the farms and fishermen behind each dish.
slots.label: 8 trends trickling down to mainstream menus

slots.sample: Not every trend belongs on every menu. We keep the ones that make our food taste better and leave the rest to others.
slots.label: 8 trends trickling down to mainstream menus

slots.sample: 8 trends trickling down to mainstream menus
slots.label: 8 trends trickling down to mainstream menus

slots.sample: A product recall at a chain the size of Starbucks makes headlines, but the way a business responds matters just as much to every restaurant, large or small.
slots.label: Starbucks faces a big recall

slots.sample: Food safety starts long before anything reaches the table: trusted suppliers, clear labelling, cold chains that are checked and logged, and a team trained to raise a concern the moment something looks wrong.
slots.label: Starbucks faces a big recall

slots.sample: In our kitchen every delivery is checked on arrival, every container is dated and every allergen is written on the prep sheet. If something ever goes wrong, we tell our guests quickly and honestly. That is how trust is kept.
slots.label: Starbucks faces a big recall

slots.sample: Reports that a casual-dining chain may be weighing bankruptcy are a sign of how hard the middle of the market has become, squeezed between fast-casual prices and fine-dining experiences.
slots.label: Logan's said to be weighing bankruptcy

slots.sample: Rising food and labour costs, rent and changing habits hit every restaurant. The ones that last tend to know exactly who they are cooking for, keep their menus focused and invest in the people who run the dining room.
slots.label: Logan's said to be weighing bankruptcy

slots.sample: We have been through a few difficult years since 1982. Each time, the answer was the same: listen to our regulars, keep the quality up and never stop giving people a reason to come back.
slots.label: Logan's said to be weighing bankruptcy

slots.sample: Logan's said to be weighing bankruptcy
slots.label: Logan's said to be weighing bankruptcy

slots.sample: Once found mostly in Southeast Asian kitchens, fish sauce is now turning up in salad dressings, marinades, burgers and even cocktails.
slots.label: Fish sauces seep onto all sorts of menus

slots.sample: A few drops add a deep, savoury note that is hard to place but easy to love. Our chefs use it in the glaze for our chili chicken, in the dressing for the grilled romaine salad and in a slow-cooked tomato sauce that tastes richer than its three ingredients.
slots.label: Fish sauces seep onto all sorts of menus

slots.sample: The trick is balance: a little acid, a little sweetness and a light hand. Used well, fish sauce does not taste of fish at all; it simply makes everything around it taste more like itself.
slots.label: Fish sauces seep onto all sorts of menus

slots.sample: Fish sauces seep onto all sorts of menus
slots.label: Fish sauces seep onto all sorts of menus

slots.sample: A pancake guarantee is a bold promise: if the stack is not right, it is on the house. It is also a smart way to show confidence in a signature dish.
slots.label: Denny’s adopts a pancake guarantee

slots.sample: Guarantees work when the kitchen can deliver them every time. That means a tested recipe, consistent equipment and cooks who know what "right" looks like.
slots.label: Denny’s adopts a pancake guarantee

slots.sample: Our own weekend brunch has a quieter promise. If anything on your plate is not as you expected, tell your server and we will make it again. It rarely happens, and when it does, it helps us get better.
slots.label: Denny’s adopts a pancake guarantee

slots.sample: Our brunch menu has a new favourite: a classic BLT built on a warm, flaky pimento cheese biscuit.
slots.label: BLT on Pimento Cheese Biscuit

slots.sample: We bake the biscuits every morning with sharp cheddar, roasted red peppers and a pinch of cayenne, then split them and layer thick-cut smoked bacon, crisp lettuce and ripe tomato with a smear of house mayonnaise.
slots.label: BLT on Pimento Cheese Biscuit

slots.sample: It is served with a side of pickled vegetables and a choice of fries or salad, Saturdays and Sundays from 10 am. Come early; the biscuits usually sell out before noon.
slots.label: BLT on Pimento Cheese Biscuit

slots.sample: Big burger chains are simplifying ingredient lists, removing artificial preservatives and colours from some of their best-known items.
slots.label: McDonald’s makes 'clean' tweaks to some menu items

slots.sample: Guests increasingly want to know what is in their food and where it comes from. That is good news for everyone who cooks from scratch.
slots.label: McDonald’s makes 'clean' tweaks to some menu items

slots.sample: At RES our sauces, dressings and stocks are made in-house, and our servers can tell you exactly what goes into every dish. "Clean" was never a trend for us; it is simply how a good kitchen works.
slots.label: McDonald’s makes 'clean' tweaks to some menu items

slots.sample: Minimum wage, tipping, tax credits and health rules: restaurant owners follow policy debates closely because the outcomes land directly on their payroll and their menus.
slots.label: How the GOP and Dems differ on restaurant issues

slots.sample: Whatever the politics, the questions every restaurant faces are practical ones. How do we pay our team fairly and keep prices our guests can afford? How do we plan when the rules may change next year?
slots.label: How the GOP and Dems differ on restaurant issues

slots.sample: We believe the answers start at home: transparent pay, clear communication with our staff and guests, and staying involved with the local business associations that speak for independent restaurants in Brooklyn.
slots.label: How the GOP and Dems differ on restaurant issues

slots.sample: RES Bar & Restaurant has been part of Brooklyn since 1982. What began as a twelve-table neighborhood bar at 4 5th Avenue is now a busy dining room, a long oak bar and a summer garden, still run with the same simple idea: cook good food from scratch and treat every guest like a regular.
slots.label: About us

slots.sample: Our menu changes with the seasons. We buy from farms in the Hudson Valley and the fish market on the waterfront, bake our bread each morning and make our pasta, sauces and desserts in-house. The bar pours local craft beer, a thoughtful wine list and classic cocktails made properly.
slots.label: About us

slots.sample: Whether you come in for a quick lunch, an after-work drink or a long dinner with friends, our team will look after you. We look forward to welcoming you.
slots.label: About us

slots.sample: Our kitchen is led by a small team of cooks who have worked together for years. They share one rule: every plate that leaves the pass should be one they would be proud to eat themselves.
slots.label: Chefs

slots.sample: Each season the team tastes, tests and argues over the new menu until every dish earns its place. Come and meet them at the chef’s counter, where you can watch dinner being cooked over the wood fire.
slots.label: Chefs
